passages.P6: # India’s exports to US, China surge in August amid stronger global trade
passages.P7: Edited by: Yashasvi Vasistha / TIMESOFINDIA.COM /  Sep 15, 2026, 22:04 IST
passages.P14: India’s exports to the US rise 21.8%, China shipments jump 52.4% in August (representative image)
passages.P15: India’s merchandise exports to the US and China recorded strong growth in August 2026, with shipments to the US rising 21.83% and those to China increasing 52.35% from a year earlier, according to commerce ministry data released on Tuesday.Exports to the US rose to $8.4 billion during the month, while shipments to China increased to $1.9 billion.Imports from both countries also grew during August, with inbound shipments from China rising 17% to $12.77 billion and those from the US jumping 65.78% to $5.97 billion.
passages.P17: During April-August 2026-27, India’s merchandise exports to the US grew 6.17% to $42.8 billion, while imports from the country increased 29.6% to $28 billion.India and the US are currently negotiating a trade pact. The US imposed an additional 10% tariff on Indian goods from July 24.Despite the tariff-related trade measures, exports to the US recorded year-on-year growth in August.
passages.P19: India’s exports to China rose 38.71% during April-August 2026-27 to $9.64 billion, while imports from China increased 27% to $65.5 billion, according to the Commerce Ministry data.The August figures showed an even sharper rise in exports to China, with shipments increasing 52.35% year-on-year to $1.9 billion.China remained a major source of imports, with India’s inbound shipments from the country reaching $12.77 billion in August.
passages.P21: India also recorded a sharp increase in exports to Singapore during August. Shipments rose 160.96% year-on-year to $1.9 billion.During the first five months of the fiscal year, exports to Singapore jumped 96.56% to $9.5 billion.Exports to Germany, South Africa, Tanzania, Australia, Malaysia, Sri Lanka and Italy also recorded positive growth during August.However, shipments to some major markets declined. Exports to the UAE fell 26.1% to $2.4 billion, which the commerce ministry attributed to the West Asia crisis.Exports to the Netherlands and Saudi Arabia also declined during the month.
